title: Esther 5
paragraphs: ¹ On the third day Esther dressed in her royal robes and stood in the inner court of the palace, facing the king's hall. The king was sitting on his royal throne in the throne room, facing the entrance. ² When he saw Queen Esther standing in the court, he was pleased with her and held out to her the golden scepter that was in his hand. Esther approached and touched the tip of the scepter. ³ "What is it, Queen Esther?" the king asked. "What is your request? I will give you up to half the kingdom." ⁴ "If it pleases the king," Esther replied, "let the king and Haman come today to a banquet I have prepared for him." ⁵ The king said, "Bring Haman quickly so that we can do what Esther has asked." So the king and Haman came to the banquet Esther had prepared.

⁶ As they were drinking wine, the king asked Esther, "Now — what is your petition? It will be granted. What is your request? Even up to half the kingdom, it will be done." ⁷ Esther replied, "My petition and my request — ⁸ if I have found favor in the king's sight and if it pleases the king to grant my petition and fulfill my request — is this: let the king and Haman come to the banquet I will prepare for them tomorrow, and then I will answer the king's question." ⁹ Haman went out that day in high spirits and in excellent humor. But when he saw Mordecai at the king's gate and noticed that Mordecai neither stood up nor moved for him, he was filled with rage at Mordecai. ¹⁰ Nevertheless, Haman restrained himself and went home. He summoned his friends and his wife Zeresh,

¹¹ and boasted to them about his vast wealth, his many sons, how the king had honored him and elevated him above all the other officials and nobles. ¹² "What's more," Haman added, "Queen Esther invited no one but me to come with the king to the banquet she had prepared — and tomorrow I am invited to join the king again. ¹³ But none of this means anything to me as long as I keep seeing that Jew Mordecai sitting at the king's gate." ¹⁴ His wife Zeresh and all his friends said to him, "Have a gallows built, seventy-five feet high, and in the morning ask the king to have Mordecai hanged on it. Then go to the banquet with the king in good spirits." Haman loved this idea, and he had the gallows built.
